messages:
oliver: Quick follow-up from the precision profiles RFC — we need to decide interface boundaries between runtime, compiler, and API for FP8/INT8/4-bit support. Who can weigh in on per-layer hints vs model-level profiles?

nina: my take: keep runtime simple. expose a model-level `precision_profile` enum (e.g. "high_quality", "balanced", "cost_opt") and let compiler/runtime map that to kernels/quant params. Per-layer hints should be optional metadata, not first-class API.

cheng: agree with nina but two caveats: 1) some models (e.g., LLaMA variants) benefit a lot from per-layer mixed precision, 2) calibration cost matters — we can't require expensive offline calibration for every profile change.

zoe: monitoring side: if we let compiler pick aggressive 4-bit paths, we must wire eval/quality signals into rollout. small perf win + big quality hit = bad. suggest automatic canary + rollback threshold for any non-"high_quality" profile.

rishi: telemetry idea: emit token-level perf/cost metrics and a lightweight delta on an eval holdout (0-1 score) so console can alert when quality drops beyond X%. keep schema tiny: profile_id, model_version, measured_p99_latency, cost_per_1k_tokens, eval_delta_pct.

oliver: Concrete proposal: API accepts `precision_profile` + optional `hints` blob. Hints are opaque key/value (e.g., "layer_12:fp16") that compiler may honor. Runtime chooses kernels based on profile and hints. Can we live with that?

nina: yes but rename `hints` -> `layer_overrides` to be clearer. and require size limit (e.g., 4KB) to avoid oversized payloads.

cheng: +1. Also add a curated set of profiles shipped with Redwood (hq, balanced, cost) and allow customers to pin a profile per deployment. For private deployments, allow an advanced toggle for per-layer overrides.

zoe: ops note: rollout plan for new profiles: 1) internal eval on standard prompt set, 2) shadow traffic for 48h with detailed telemetry, 3) canary 1%, 5%, 25% with auto-rollback. Document this in console rollout UI.

rishi: I'll draft the telemetry schema and add it to the profiling RFC. also propose a simple UI in console to compare profiles side-by-side (latency/cost/quality).

oliver: sample config we'd accept in API payload:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-7b",
  "precision_profile": "balanced",
  "layer_overrides": {"layer_10": "fp16", "layer_29": "int8"},
  "quality_slo_pct": "98"
}
```

cheng: note: we should define semantics for "auto" fallback: if runtime detects large divergence in logits after quant path, should it fallback to higher precision automatically or mark request degraded? I vote auto-fallback + increment counter for visibility.

nina: auto-fallback ok but must be rate-limited to avoid spinning to slow path under load. add cooldown and per-client budget.

zoe: add an audit log entry whenever fallback happens (model/profile, request_id, reason) so support can triage.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-3412: "precision-profile API + telemetry + rollout plan" assigned to @rishi, @cheng, @nina.

oliver: action items: rishi -> telemetry schema draft by EOD Tue; cheng -> doc for compiler hints and per-layer semantics by Thu; nina -> API + size limits and consent for private deployments by Thu; zoe -> rollout checklist for console by Fri. we'll sync in 30m. Thanks. :thumbsup:
